summary.title: Robustness of the extraction
summary.text: With the ICPAC map as digitized and shifted by one source pixel in each direction, the All Ethiopia category agreement stays between 38.3% and 41.8%. With the ICPAC map as digitized and shifted by one source pixel in each direction, the FMAM R2 (Belg) rainfall domain category agreement stays between 17.5% and 27.4%. These are bounded sensitivity checks of the extraction, not statistical confidence intervals; exact EMI zone comparisons remain unavailable.

paragraphs.text: The platform does not show a unique favoured category over EMI zone West under its applicable rule. EMI prints 25% / 30% / 45% (below / near / above). Over the whole zone (as digitized from the EMI figure), the platform area mean is 33% / 32% / 35%: no clear category in one source.

The platform does not show a unique favoured category over EMI zone North-central under its applicable rule. EMI prints 10% / 30% / 60% (below / near / above). Over the whole zone (as digitized from the EMI figure), the platform area mean is 35% / 32% / 33%: no clear category in one source.

The platform does not show a unique favoured category over EMI zone South-central under its applicable rule. EMI prints 15% / 30% / 55% (below / near / above). Over the whole zone (as digitized from the EMI figure), the platform area mean is 38% / 31% / 31%: no clear category in one source.

The platform does not show a unique favoured category over EMI zone Southeast under its applicable rule. EMI prints 20% / 35% / 45% (below / near / above). Over the whole zone (as digitized from the EMI figure), the platform area mean is 33% / 31% / 36%: no clear category in one source.

The EMI zones were digitized from the figure's fill colours and placed by fitting the country outline, so their boundaries are approximate; the figure states no reference period, so probability differences are not calculated.

The outlooks favour different categories over much of their shared displayed area in Ethiopia. ICPAC shows a favoured category on 89% of Ethiopia and no forecast category shown (the legend does not explain the grey areas) on 11%; where it shows one it favours above normal on 69%, most often at 40-50% and 33-40%. The platform favours above normal on 8% and below normal on 12% of Ethiopia. There is category agreement of 40.7% within the compared area, which covers 22% of the analysed national area; opposite categories (above vs below) on 21% of the compared area. ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its probability interval, so probabilities are not differenced. The official outlook covers Mar 2026–May 2026 and the platform Feb 2026–May 2026 (Feb 2026 only in the platform), so this compares spatial tendencies, not probabilities for the same seasonal event.

The outlooks favour different categories over much of their shared displayed area in the FMAM R2 (Belg) rainfall domain. ICPAC shows a favoured category on 90% of the FMAM R2 (Belg) rainfall domain and no forecast category shown (the legend does not explain the grey areas) on 10%; where it shows one it favours above normal on 79%, most often at 40-50% and 33-40%. The platform favours above normal on <1% and below normal on 4% of the FMAM R2 (Belg) rainfall domain. There is category agreement of 24.9% within the compared area, which covers 10% of the analysed domain; opposite categories (above vs below) on 30% of the compared area. ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its probability interval, so probabilities are not differenced. The official outlook covers Mar 2026–May 2026 and the platform Feb 2026–May 2026 (Feb 2026 only in the platform), so this compares spatial tendencies, not probabilities for the same seasonal event.

Not calculated: rainfall-anomaly differences, because no official rainfall-amount anomaly product was found in the checked ICPAC and EMI products; which forecast is more accurate, because that needs observations and a separate verification design (see Verification); same-event probability differences, because the target windows or spatial supports differ and ICPAC publishes only favoured-category intervals.

Favoured category: the leading tercile where it reaches 40% (the map display rule); otherwise no clear category.
An OND probability cannot be built by averaging monthly probabilities; ONDJ and OND are compared only as spatial tendencies.
